problems.statement: One item costs $d$ dollars, and a second item costs $2d$ dollars. I get a 4% discount on the first item and a 10% discount on the second. What is my overall discount?
Jo buys 2 gal of gas and 2 qt of oil. A gallon of gas costs \$1.20 more than a quart of oil; the price per qt of oil is 60% of the price per gal of gas. How much does Jo pay?
Given $\triangle BCE$ in the figure at the right, if $m\angle ABC = x^\circ$, $m\angle DCE = (x + 10)^\circ$, and $m\angle BEF = (x - 15)^\circ$, in which interval below does the value of $x$ lie?
Ed has an equal number of dimes and nickels and no pennies. After spending 15¢, he has twice as many dimes as nickels. How many nickels did he have originally?
Let $A$ and $B$ be single nonzero digits, so that $AA$ is a 2-digit number with identical digits. Which of the following is a value of $A$ which satisfies $AA + A = B * A^B$?

Each member of a group of 5 people is either a knight, who always tells the truth, or a knave, who always lies. Each member of the group looks at everyone else in the group, and then one member says, “I see at least one person who sees only knaves.” What is the least possible number of knights in the group?
There are exactly 2 noncongruent rectangular boxes with integer-length edges whose space diagonals have length 17. Find the ratio of the larger to the smaller volume.

A positive integer $N$ leaves the remainder $r \ne 0$ when divided into any of 527, 622, and 698. A different positive integer $M$ leaves the remainder $s \ne 0$ when divided into any of 736, 881, and 997. Find $M + N$.
The three-digit number $abc$ is 29 times the sum of its digits, the number $bca$ is 68 times the sum of its digits, and the number $cab$ is 14 times the sum of its digits. Find $a + 2b + 3c$.

In $\triangle SML$, $SM = 8$, $ML = 12$, and $LS = 18$. Of the 3 sides and 3 angles of $\triangle SML$, five of these parts are congruent to five parts of $\triangle TYC$, but $\triangle SML$ is NOT congruent to $\triangle TYC$. If the sides of $\triangle TYC$ are all integers, find the longest side of $\triangle TYC$.

Every integer $N > 0$ can be represented in at least one way as $ab - (a + b)$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive integers with $a \le b$. Find the least $N$ having at least 3 such representations, and write your answer on the answer sheet.
What is the remainder when $x^{2000} - 2x^{15} + 2$ is divided by $x^2 - 1$?
Find all values of $k$ such that the equation $\log (kx) = 2 \log (x + 1)$ has exactly one real solution.
In the system of equations $\begin{cases} xy + z = 105 \\ x + yz = 107 \end{cases}$, for how many integer values of $y$ does the system have a solution in integers?
In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A = 30^\circ$, $\angle C = 90^\circ$, and $AB = 2\sqrt{6}$. Let $D$ be the point on side $AB$ such that segment $CD$ bisects $\angle C$. Find $CD$.
If $\sin x \cos x = 4 \sin x + 4 \cos x$, $\sin 2x$ can be represented in the form $a + b\sqrt{c}$, where $a$, $b$, and $c$ are integers and $c$ is a prime number. Find $a + b + c$.

A circle with center $O$ has radius 10 and is tangent to $\angle BAC$ at points $B$ and $C$. A circle with center $Q$ is tangent to the first circle at $P$ and to $\angle BAC$ at $D$ and $E$. A circle with center $S$ is tangent to the second circle at $R$ and to $\angle BAC$ at $F$ and $G$. If $OP > QR > RS$ and $OA = 25$, find $\sqrt{AS}$.
Let $a + b = M$ and $ab = N$. The polynomial $a^4 + b^4$ can be represented as $PM^4 - QM^2N + RN^2$, where $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are positive integers. Find $P + Q + R$.
If order doesn’t matter, find the number of ways that 2016 can be written as the product of 3 positive integers. For example, one product would be $12 * 12 * 14 = 12 * 14 * 12 = 14 * 12 * 12$.

Let the set $S$ be the empty set. Add the elements of $\{1, 2\}$ to $S$, and after 1 minute randomly remove 1 element of $S$. Next add the 4 elements of $\{3, 4, 5, 6\}$ to $S$ and after 30 sec randomly remove 2 of the 5 elements of $S$. Continue this process forever, each time doubling the number of elements added and removed and halving the time. To the nearest hundredth of a minute, find the average length of time 1 remains in $S$.
